summary.text: 里 is traditionally analyzed as 田 plus 土, interpreted as a habitable place or settlement. It is also attested as a distance measure. A reported bronze use writes 裏, “lining”; this is proposed sound-based borrowing, though the depicted referent’s old name and pronunciation are not established.

formation.text: Semantic compound: 田 and 土 depict field and earth in the traditional interpretation of a habitable place. The selected Western Zhou bronze-style image illustrates this analysis; it is a modern redraw, not an artifact image.

components.text: 田 is the field element in the traditional analysis. Reported bronze forms show strokes in 田 and 土 running together; no distinct earlier form for 田 is specified.
土 is the earth element in the traditional analysis. In reported later forms, its dot extends into a short stroke in forms underlying seal script.

history.text: The graph is reported in Western Zhou bronze inscriptions. Later bronze forms show strokes in 田 and 土 running together, and a dot in 土 extended into a short stroke in forms underlying seal script. The selected bronze-style illustration is a modern vector redraw.

One reported bronze inscription uses 里 to write 裏 in a phrase about a garment lining. This is proposed sound-based borrowing: the sign was reused for a different word because the words may have sounded alike. The old referent’s name and pronunciation are not established, so the sound match remains uncertain.

Early reported uses include a settlement-related title and a distance measure; later manuscript examples include settlement, distance, and 理. These attestations do not establish when each sense began or a semantic chain connecting them.

uncertainties.text: The 田-plus-土 account is a traditional interpretation of a habitable place, not proof of the graph’s precise original referent. Proposed links between the village word and Proto-Sino-Tibetan forms or 理 are not verified here.

The reported Western Zhou graph attestation does not establish the earliest pronunciation or first occurrence of each word sense. The cited artifact images and primary editions were not independently examined.

The distance and interior uses lack a securely established first occurrence or semantic connection to the settlement sense. The sound analysis of 里 in 裏 supports its phonetic role there, but does not establish 里’s earliest pronunciation or original referent.

senses.period: Western Zhou bronze inscriptions (earliest reported graph attestation; exact first sense occurrence unresolved)
senses.text: The traditional account glosses 里 as habitation, and a Western Zhou bronze use for a settlement-related title is reported. This supports an early settlement sense, though the precise original referent remains interpretive.

senses.period: attested in bronze inscriptions; first emergence unresolved
senses.text: A bronze use for a distance measure is reported. It establishes an attestation, not when the sense began or how it relates to settlement.

senses.gloss: inside or interior, in the use associated with 裏/裡
senses.text: 里 is reported writing 裏 in a bronze phrase about garment lining. This is use of the graph to write another word, not evidence that “inside” developed from the settlement sense. The interior sense is associated with 裏/裡 in later usage.

senses.period: attested in historical uses; first emergence unresolved
senses.text: Village and neighborhood are recorded senses, with settlement uses reported in early sources. The evidence does not establish a dated development from habitation to village or neighborhood.

developments.text: In a reported bronze inscription, 里 writes 裏 in a garment-lining phrase. The proposed mechanism is reuse of the sign for a different word because their pronunciations were similar; the old referent’s name and pronunciation are not established. This is graph borrowing, not a shift from settlement to lining.

limitations.text: The reported settlement, distance, and interior uses do not establish each sense’s first occurrence or a semantic chain among them. The interior example shows 里 used to write 裏; it does not show that 里’s settlement meaning changed into “lining” or “inside.”

The phonetic analysis of 里 within 裏 does not establish 里’s earliest pronunciation or original referent. The proposed whole-graph borrowing therefore has a qualified sound mechanism, not a demonstrated comparison with the original referent’s name.

overview.text: 里 combines a field and earth in a traditional interpretation of a habitable place or settlement. It also writes a distance measure. In one reported inscription it writes 裏, “lining,” apparently because the words sounded alike, though the old referent’s name and sound are uncertain.

components.text: 田 depicts a field, contributing the field element in the traditional explanation of a settlement.
土 depicts earth, contributing the earth element in that explanation.

takeaway.text: The bronze use of 里 for 裏 is proposed sound-based borrowing, not evidence that “lining” developed from the settlement meaning.

relationships.text: In the reported 田-plus-土 analysis of 里, 田 depicts a field and contributes that pictured element to the habitable-place interpretation.
In the reported 田-plus-土 analysis of 里, 土 depicts earth and contributes that pictured element to the habitable-place interpretation.

里 is analyzed as the phonetic element in 裏. Both have current Mandarin reading lǐ and are reported in the same Middle Chinese category 來開三之上. This supports the phonetic analysis within 裏, not the old referent or earliest pronunciation of 里. The reported Japanese on-reading ri for both is not evidence for the Chinese historical origin.

裡 is reported as a later alternative form of 裏, a variant relation rather than a standardized simplification. This relationship connects the related graph to this entry’s reported bronze use of 里 for 裏.
